meta.title: SiteSeer for industry: train your team on the building first
meta.description: RFIs and defects cost the industry time and money. SiteSeer trains your team on the actual building in 3D, at every stage, before they build it.

hero.statement: Train your team on the building before they build it. RFIs and defects cost time and money; SiteSeer shows every stage in 3D, matched 1-to-1 with what gets built.

steps.line: Every trade, in the order they build.
Understand the detail before it becomes an RFI.

inspect.title: Lintel bearing
inspect.text: How far does the lintel bear each side of the opening? Answered on the model, before anyone has to ask.

inspect.title: Weep holes over the head
inspect.text: Where do the weep holes go above a window? Shown in place, in the course above the lintel.

steps.line: See where a defect starts, and how to avoid it.

pulls.kicker: Common defect · Damp at the sill
pulls.title: Cavity tray lap
pulls.text: With the veneer pulled back, see how the tray flashing should lap and drain to the weep holes.

pulls.title: Head flashing
pulls.text: Recorded against the layer: the head detail relies on the flashing, not the sealant.

steps.line: Walk the site before day one.

problem.heading: RFIs and defects are expensive.
problem.lede: Most start with someone on site not understanding how a detail goes together, because drawings don't show the sequence. SiteSeer trains your team on the actual building, at every stage, before they build it.

points.title: Fewer RFIs.
points.text: Staff see the detail in 3D, at the stage it is built, before they need to ask.

points.title: Fewer defects.
points.text: They see what gets covered up, and what it relies on, before it is covered.

points.title: Confidence on site.
points.text: The model matches 1-to-1 with what gets built, so what they learned is what they will find.

problem.alt: A bolted steel knee connection where a portal frame rafter meets its column
problem.caption: A portal frame connection, bolted as it is fabricated.

how.heading: Pause the build. Walk in.
how.lede: Pick a stage and step inside it. Try the buttons on the wall: this is the same idea, on a whole building.

points.title: We build the staged model.
points.text: From your architectural or shop-drawing models, or as a custom build by our team.

points.title: Your team walks it.
points.text: Every stage, in real time, on the machines they already use.

points.title: Inspection points explain it.
points.text: What each detail is, what it relies on, and where it tends to go wrong.

strip.alt: A timber wall frame standing on a slab beside a site workbench
strip.caption: The frame, before the lining goes on.

strip.alt: A raking-ceiling room with blue sarking and insulation exposed between the framing
strip.caption: Sarking and insulation, before they're covered.

strip.alt: A two-storey house mid-construction on a suburban site
strip.caption: The whole house, part way through the build.

uses.heading: Training on the building they're about to build.
uses.lede: Not a generic course: your project, at every stage.

items.title: Walk the site before day one.
items.text: New crews see the site, the sequence and the hazards before they arrive.

items.title: Layer by layer.
items.text: Each tricky detail taken apart and put back together, in the order it is built.

items.title: Where it goes wrong.
items.text: Common defects shown where they happen, with what prevents them.

items.title: What a detail relies on.
items.text: Recorded against the model, where the next trade will see it.

access.heading: In the office and on site.
access.lede: On the machines your team already has, at the desk and at the slab edge.

ways.title: In the office
ways.text: Runs on the Windows and macOS machines your team already uses.

ways.title: On site
ways.text: Web versions run in the browser on iOS and Android tablets and phones, at the slab edge.

ways.title: In the browser
ways.text: Share a model with the browser viewer, with nothing to install.

ways.title: Site inductions
ways.text: Run it on any PC in the site office to walk new crews through the site.

results.heading: Proven in the classroom, now on site.
results.lede: SiteSeer began in construction education, where a building has to make sense to someone who has never seen it built. That's what a site team needs too.

outcomes.title: Shared understanding.
outcomes.text: Everyone looks at the same element at the same stage.

outcomes.title: Earlier answers.
outcomes.text: Questions are raised against the model before the trade arrives.

outcomes.title: One place to look.
outcomes.text: The question, the element and the stage, together.

contact.heading: See it on your build.
contact.lede: Book a walkthrough, or talk to us about training your team on a live project.
